title: Microsoft Scout - Simply Explained

entities.name: AI agent
entities.quote: Scout is a desktop agent that monitors your work and acts on its own.

entities.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
entities.quote: Scout also supports MCP servers. Don't let the acronym scare you.

entities.name: Agent skill
entities.quote: Scout can also be taught skills. These are reusable recipes for common tasks.

entities.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
entities.quote: So you've probably heard someone say co-pilot and co-work and scout all in the same sentence.

entities.name: Copilot Cowork

entities.name: Microsoft 365
entities.quote: Scout connects to three worlds. First, Microsoft 365, your email calendar, Teams chats and SharePoint files.

quotes.text: Co-pilot and co-work both wait for you to initiate. You start the conversation, you give the task, scout doesn't wait. It watches, it monitors, it acts on its own.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the defining difference between Copilot, Cowork and Scout.

quotes.text: When co-pilot acts, it acts as you. It uses your permissions, your access, your identity. When scout acts, it has its own identity. It's a separate digital worker with its own permissions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why agent identity matters for security.

quotes.text: This is not just a minor upgrade to co-pilot. It's a fundamental shift in how AI works with you. Co-pilot is a tool you use. Scout is an agent that works alongside you.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames Scout as a shift from tool to agent.

quotes.text: The identity model, the permission structures, the approval workflows you design now will apply to future agents.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Argues for starting agent governance before Scout is generally available.

quotes.text: Everything you learn on Copilot and cowork transfers directly to Scout. The skills you build today will work tomorrow.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a practical reason to invest in Copilot and Cowork skills now.

chapters.title: How Scout works under the hood

takeaways: Scout is Microsoft's first Autopilot: unlike Copilot and Cowork, it acts proactively on schedules and triggers without waiting for a prompt.
Scout runs as a desktop app under its own identity, connects to Microsoft 365 via Work IQ, local files, the web and MCP servers, and gates sensitive actions with approvals.
Scout is in private Frontier preview and needs Microsoft 365 Copilot, a GitHub Copilot license and Intune policies, so organizations should start with Copilot, Cowork skills and agent governance now.
hook: Copilot, Cowork and Scout sound like alphabet soup to most Microsoft 365 users and IT leaders. This episode explains in plain English what Microsoft Scout is, how its always-on Autopilot model differs from Copilot, what it needs in licensing and why preparing agent governance now pays off.
